title: Elderflower infusion for sinus congestion
subtitle: A hot diaphoretic cup for a blocked nose
excerpt: A hot elderflower infusion for sinus congestion and a blocked nose. The heat and the herb's anti-catarrhal action work together; the infusion must be taken hot to make the most of this. Two teaspoons of dried flowers per 250 ml, steeped covered for ten minutes. No significant safety concerns for most readers.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), elderflower entry: notes the diaphoretic and anti-catarrhal use of hot elderflower infusion for colds and catarrhal conditions of the nose. Culpeper, The English Physician (1652), elder entry: records use of the flowers for head colds and blocked sinuses. BHP (1983) elderflower monograph: dosing reference.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dried elderflower stores 12 months in a sealed tin away from light. Prepare each cup fresh and drink it while still hot.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Prepare fresh for each dose. Drink while hot. Do not store the brewed infusion.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation made by pouring just-boiled water over leaves or flowers and steeping them covered, so the volatile oils stay in the cup rather than escaping with the steam.
A herb that promotes gentle perspiration, traditionally used to support the body's own response to a fever or heavy cold, and to encourage the release of catarrh.

content.text: Hot elderflower infusion is a clear, honey-scented cup of dried elderflowers steeped in just-off-the-boil water, traditionally drunk hot at the first sign of a blocked nose or sinus congestion during a cold. The heat itself helps; the flowers carry a

and anti-catarrhal action that western herbalists draw on specifically in hot preparations: a cold infusion or cold elderflower drink is pleasant but this is not it. Two teaspoons of dried flowers per 250 ml, steeped covered for ten minutes, makes one strong cup. It should be drunk while still hot. Dried elderflowers keep 12 months in a sealed tin away from light.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body:
Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms.

Elderflower (the flower of Sambucus nigra) has no significant safety concerns at the doses described here for most readers. The flower is distinct from the berry: elderberries must always be cooked before use as raw berries contain cyanogenic glycosides, but the flowers at infusion doses do not share this concern.

Foraging note: if using fresh foraged elderflowers rather than dried purchased herb, be confident in the identification. Elder (Sambucus nigra) has flat-topped white flower heads that smell distinctly of elderflower. Dwarf elder (Sambucus ebulus) has a similar appearance but a much less pleasant, rank smell and is toxic. If in doubt, use dried herb from a reputable supplier.

Paediatric use is not adult-divided-by-half. Consult a herbalist who specialises in children's herbal medicine, or a paediatric doctor, before using any herbal preparation in children under twelve.

content.text: Put 2 teaspoons of dried elderflowers into a teapot or a cup with a lid.
Pour over 250 ml of just-off-the-boil water and cover immediately.
Steep covered for 10 minutes. The water turns very pale straw-coloured and smells of elderflower.
Strain through a sieve and drink while still hot. This preparation works best when hot.
One hot cup (250 ml) two to three times a day, for the duration of the congestion, up to seven days. Drink while hot each time. If symptoms worsen or a fever develops, see your doctor.
Prepare each cup fresh. Dried elderflowers store in a sealed tin or jar away from light and heat for up to 12 months.
When not to use this remedy

See a doctor for congestion with high fever, severe facial pain, swelling around the eyes, or symptoms that worsen after ten days of cold-like illness. These can indicate sinusitis or another condition that needs treatment.

items.symptom: Little flavour or aroma from the infusion
items.cause: Dried elderflowers are old or have been stored in the light
items.fix: Replace with fresh dried elderflowers. Good dried elderflower should smell clearly honey-floral when rubbed between the fingers.

items.cause: Herb has gone off, or jar was not clean
items.fix: Discard and start with fresh dried herb in a clean sealed container.
